newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland meat imports seen up 40,000 T in 97 -agency.
newsitem.headline: Poland meat imports seen up 40,000 T in 97 -agency.

text.p: The government's food market regulator, the Agriculture Market Agency (ARR), said in a forecast that Poland's meat imports are likely to rise to 150,000 tonnes in 1997 from 110,000 tonnes this year.
"It is estimated that to fill supply gaps in 1997, meat imports should rise to 150,000 tonnes from this year's expected 110,000 tonnes," the forecast, dated November 12, said.
The ARR said that pork bellies were expected to make up about 90,000 tonnes of next year's imports.
It also said that a duty-free import quota may have to be created next year in order to compensate for the high prices of pork bellies on international markets.
"Due to the high level of pork prices on foreign markets an appropriate duty-free import quota is necessary," the ARR said.
It also said that due to the low profitability of livestock in Poland stemming from the high price of fodder grains, meat exports were likely to be halved next year to about 100,000 tonnes.
The ARR said livestock production as a whole would likely fall by around six percent next year.

Polish procurement pork prices were expected to rise by about 10 percent next year to about 4.3-4.5 zlotys/kilogramme in December. In 1996 meat prices are expected to rise by about 25 percent. --Robert Bogdanski +48 22 653 9700
